content: Write a regex that matches an ISO 8601 date like 2026-10-01.

```regex
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

It matches `2026-10-01` and rejects out-of-range months and days like `2026-13-01` and `2026-10-32`.

- `\d{4}` is the year.
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])` is the month, 01–12.
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])` is the day, 01–31.

To find dates inside longer text, swap the anchors for `\b`:

```regex
\b\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])\b
```

A regex can't tell that `2026-02-30` isn't a real date, because it doesn't know month lengths or leap years. If you need that, parse the string with a date library after the regex check.
